title: Children's data - the special obligations companies must follow
p1: A child clicking “accept” online may not fully understand what they are agreeing to. So why do companies have stricter rules when collecting children's data?
p2: Many people think privacy rules treat all users the same. The surprising truth is that children's personal information often receives extra protection because young users may not recognize risks or understand how their data can be used.
p3: Companies that collect children's data may need stronger safeguards, clearer explanations, and proper consent processes. They must avoid practices that take advantage of a child's lack of experience, such as pushing unnecessary data collection or using confusing privacy notices. The practical takeaway: protecting children's information is not just about compliance; it is about building safer digital spaces for younger users.
